**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/25 (Thu) 13:29
- [USER] User inquired about calculating VAT of a shopping list in the Philippines.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To calculate the VAT in the Philippines, the VAT rate is currently 12%.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The VAT can be calculated by multiplying the total cost of the items by the VAT rate in decimal form.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Example provided: If the total cost of items is PHP 1000, the VAT would be calculated as 1000 x 0.12 = PHP 120.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Total cost of items including VAT would be PHP 1,120 (1000 + 120).
- [USER] User asked if all stores need to include VAT in their invoices in the Philippines.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In the Philippines, businesses that are VAT-registered are required to include VAT in their invoices.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] VAT-registered businesses are those whose annual sales or gross receipts exceed PHP 3 million.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] VAT-registered businesses must charge VAT on their sales and include it in the invoices issued to customers.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] VAT-registered businesses are required to file VAT returns and pay the VAT collected to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Businesses that are not VAT-registered (annual sales or gross receipts below PHP 3 million) are not required to charge and include VAT in their invoices.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Not all stores need to include VAT in their invoices; it depends on the store's VAT registration status and annual sales or gross receipts.
